outcome: I found no posting since 26 January 2024 that characterises all word-representable graphs by (induced) forbidden subgraphs. The window holds forbidden-subgraph characterisations of restricted classes only: split graphs with an independent set of size 4 (Roy and Hariharasubramanian, arXiv July 2025, Utilitas Mathematica online July 2026), co-bipartite graphs with one clique of size at most 4 (Chen, Hameed and Kitaev, arXiv August 2025, Discussiones Mathematicae Graph Theory 2025/26), and two arXiv-only preprints from December 2025 (Srinivasan and Hariharasubramanian) that give infinite-family forbidden-subgraph characterisations of semi-transitive split graphs and of word-representable co-bipartite graphs. Wikipedia (last edited 9 August 2026) still lists the general problem as open, and the July 2026 journal version of the split-graph paper says a complete classification remains open.
problem_asks: Read from the statement alone, the bullet asks for (1) a characterisation of the word-representable graphs (graphs admitting a word in which two letters alternate exactly when their vertices are adjacent; equivalently graphs with a semi-transitive orientation) (2) in terms of (induced) forbidden subgraphs: a list of forbidden graphs such that a graph is word-representable if and only if it contains none of them. The class is hereditary, so the natural form is its minimal non-word-representable induced subgraphs. The statement does not say the list must be finite, and it does not restrict the graph class, the number of vertices, or any clique or independent-set size. The bracketed '(induced)' is read as indicating that induced subgraphs are the intended form, while the bullet names both. The bullet is one universal claim about all graphs, with no separate parts.

events.what_happened: Kitaev, Long, Ma and Wu posted 'Word-representability of split graphs'. Per the arXiv abstract (opened), they characterise in terms of forbidden subgraphs the word-representable split graphs in which independent-set vertices have degree at most 2, or in which the clique has size 4, and they give conditions for a split-graph orientation to be semi-transitive. The abstract says almost nothing was known about split graphs at that time. The journal version (Journal of Combinatorics 12(4), listed on Strathclyde's record) is not opened. The Roy and Hariharasubramanian paper also credits this group with the independent-set-size-3 case (its Theorem 2.13), which the arXiv abstract does not state.
events.revisions: v1 only on arXiv (27 Sep 2017). Journal of Combinatorics 12(4) per Strathclyde record (year given inconsistently as 2021 or 2022).
events.delivers: Restricted to split graphs: a forbidden-subgraph characterisation of word-representable split graphs with independent-set degree at most 2, and of those with clique size 4. Nothing for graphs outside split graphs.
events.remains: All non-split graphs; split graphs outside the two stated cases (for example clique size 5 or more with unrestricted independent-set degree); the general forbidden-subgraph characterisation.

events.what_happened: Akgün, Gent, Kitaev and Zantema posted 'Solving computational problems in the theory of word-representable graphs'. Per the arXiv abstract (opened), they used semi-transitive orientations to enumerate all connected non-word-representable graphs up to 11 vertices, reporting about three CPU-years of computation; they also determined the distribution of k-representable graphs on up to 9 vertices and report that the enumeration led to a correction of a published result (not named in the abstract). Published in the Journal of Integer Sequences 22 (2019), article 19.2.5. The solver names (Savile Row, Minion, geng) come from a search snippet; the abstract does not name them.

events.delivers: A finite census: all connected non-word-representable graphs on at most 11 vertices, computed by exhaustive search over semi-transitive orientations. This is finitely many instances of a claim about all graphs. It gives no characterisation and no bound on the size of minimal forbidden subgraphs.
events.remains: The characterisation for all graph sizes; the complete list of minimal non-word-representable graphs beyond the census range. Wikipedia lists the complete list as open.

events.what_happened: Chen, Kitaev and Saito posted 'Representing split graphs by words'. Per the arXiv abstract (opened), threshold graphs are word-representable; split graphs with clique size 5 are characterised computationally by nine forbidden subgraphs, extending the clique-size-4 case; and gluing two word-representable graphs along a clique of size at least 2 may or may not give a word-representable graph, which answers a question open for about ten years. Published in Discussiones Mathematicae Graph Theory 42(4) (2022), pp. 1263-1280, per the reference list of Roy and Hariharasubramanian (the DMGT page itself was not opened).
events.revisions: v1 only on arXiv (20 Sep 2019). DMGT 42(4) 2022.
events.delivers: Restricted to split graphs with clique size 5: a computational forbidden-subgraph characterisation (nine graphs, given in the paper as T1 to T8 and T9 per the Roy paper's summary). Also threshold graphs word-representable, and the gluing result. Nothing outside split graphs.
events.remains: Split graphs with clique size 6 or more; all non-split graphs; the general characterisation.

events.object: Nine forbidden induced subgraphs for word-representable split graphs with clique size 5 (their exact graphs were not extracted from the paper; the Roy paper refers to them as T1 to T8 and T9).

events.what_happened: Kitaev and Pyatkin posed 'On semi-transitive orientability of split graphs' on arXiv. Per the arXiv abstract (opened), recognising semi-transitive orientability of split graphs can be done in polynomial time (the general problem is NP-complete), and they characterise, by minimal forbidden induced subgraphs, the semi-transitively orientable split graphs whose independent set has size at most 3, extending a known classification for clique size at most 5. The paper was published in Information Processing Letters 184 (2024), article 106435, which is the '2024' version cited later. The Roy paper says this paper poses the open problem for independent-set size 4. The matrix (circular-ones) criterion attributed to this paper in a search snippet does not appear in the arXiv abstract; the Srinivasan paper states it as Theorem 4.1, derived from Kitaev and Pyatkin's Theorems 4 and 5.
events.revisions: v1 only on arXiv (17 Oct 2021). Information Processing Letters 184 (2024), article 106435; the search result gives online publication 1 Sept 2023.
events.delivers: Restricted to split graphs: polynomial-time recognition of semi-transitive split graphs; a forbidden-induced-subgraph characterisation of semi-transitive split graphs with independent set of size at most 3. Nothing outside split graphs.
events.remains: Split graphs with independent set of size 4 or more (the case the Roy paper and the Utilitas journal version treat as open or as posed by these authors); all non-split graphs; the general characterisation.

events.what_happened: Kitaev and Sun posted 'Human-verifiable proofs in the theory of word-representable graphs'. Per the arXiv abstract (opened), they describe publicly available software that automatically produces short checkable proofs that specific graphs are not word-representable, using failures of semi-transitive orientations. Applied to the Shrikhande graph (a 6-line proof) and the Clebsch graph (a 10-line proof). A RAIRO-ITA 2024 publication appears in search results (not opened).

events.direction: Two non-word-representable graphs with certificates. Consistent with the existence of minimal forbidden graphs; neither way on a characterisation.
events.object: Shrikhande graph and Clebsch graph, both 16 vertices, each shown non-word-representable by a short proof from the software. Explicit certificates are proofs generated by the software, not closed-form constructions.

events.what_happened: Das and Hariharasubramanian posted 'Square-free word-representation of word-representable graphs'. Per the arXiv abstract (opened), every non-empty word-representable graph has a representing word with no non-trivial squares, which the abstract says answers an open problem from Kitaev and Lozin's book. Also: minimal-length representing words are square-free, square-free representations of complete graphs are counted, and infinitely many square-free words (from the Thue-Morse sequence) represent a non-complete connected word-representable graph.
events.revisions: v1 only on arXiv (22 Feb 2024). Graphs and Combinatorics 42:12 (2026), per the arXiv journal reference.
events.delivers: Square-free representability of every non-empty word-representable graph. This is about the representing words, not the graph class or its forbidden subgraphs.
events.remains: The whole bullet.

Per the arXiv abstract (opened), they determine the minimum length of word-representants for Cartesian and rooted products, and claim to resolve Broere's open problem on constructing a word for the Cartesian product of two arbitrary word-representable graphs.

events.what_happened: Srinivasan and Hariharasubramanian posted 'On semi-transitive orientability of circulant graphs'. Per the arXiv abstract (opened), Kitaev and Pyatkin had shown every 4-regular circulant graph is semi-transitive and posed an open problem on circulant graphs whose connection set is a run of consecutive positive integers; the authors say they solve it. They also report results on some k-regular circulants with k of at least 5 (semi-transitive under some assumptions, non-semi-transitive for others) and bounds on the representation number of some k-regular circulants. Published in Discrete Applied Mathematics 377 (2025), pp. 498-509, per the arXiv journal reference.

events.remains: The whole bullet: a forbidden-subgraph characterisation of all word-representable graphs. Circulants in general are not characterised.

Per the journal abstract (opened), they bring in tools from posets, Ramsey theory, finite geometry and probabilistic methods, and settle several open problems on the existence and length of word-representations for various graph classes. The journal page lists publication on 4 Oct 2024. The journal page does not give a preprint date. The NSF public-access record, which a search snippet reports as submitted 16 Feb 2024, could not be read.

events.what_happened: Das and Hariharasubramanian posted 'Word-representability of co-bipartite graph' (co-bipartite: vertex set partitioned into two cliques). Per the arXiv abstract (opened), they give necessary and sufficient conditions for a co-bipartite graph to have a semi-transitive orientation (equivalent to word-representability), with partial results: co-bipartite graphs with one clique partition of size 2 are word-representable, and complements of paths, even cycles and generalised crown graphs are word-representable. The abstract quotes Kitaev and Lozin's book that characterising word-representable co-bipartite graphs remains open; it does not claim to solve that. No forbidden-subgraph list appears in the abstract.
events.revisions: v1 only on arXiv (17 Jan 2025). No journal reference listed.
events.delivers: For co-bipartite graphs: conditions in terms of semi-transitive orientations, plus partial cases. No forbidden-subgraph form.
events.remains: A forbidden-subgraph characterisation of co-bipartite graphs; the general class.
events.doubts: The later Srinivasan and Hariharasubramanian preprint (2512.12274) credits Das and Hariharasubramanian with 'a complete characterization in terms of necessary and sufficient conditions' and cites this arXiv number. The arXiv page I opened lists only v1 and its abstract states conditions for semi-transitive orientation, not completeness. The attribution is recorded in disputes.
events.direction: Restricted class (co-bipartite) in a non-forbidden-subgraph form. Cuts neither way on the forbidden-subgraph claim.

events.remains: The whole bullet.
events.direction: Neighbouring question (representation number). Cuts neither way on forbidden subgraphs.

events.what_happened: Kenkireth, Sajith and Sasidharan posted 'Word-representability and comparability: minimal forbidden induced subgraphs and cover number bounds'. Per the arXiv abstract (opened), they identify which minimal non-comparability graphs are also minimal non-word-representable; they give a complete description of minimal non-word-representable graphs containing an all-adjacent vertex; they show the universal O(log n) cover-number bound for word-representable graphs by comparability graphs is tight. The abstract says the characterisation for word-representable graphs remains open.
events.revisions: v1 10 Feb 2025; v2 27 Apr 2026; v3 14 May 2026; v4 17 Jun 2026 (current). Journal status not found.

events.remains: Minimal non-word-representable graphs with no all-adjacent vertex; the general characterisation.
events.doubts: A search snippet (not verified in the full text) says a family stated in a preliminary version as non-word-representable for all n of at least 2 was corrected in a later version. The arXiv listing shows four versions. I did not compare them, so I cannot say whether the all-adjacent-vertex list changed between versions. Scope that changed between versions is a point for the later pass.

events.what_happened: Roy and Hariharasubramanian posted 'Word-representability of split graphs with independent set of size 4' (arXiv 2507.08483, 11 July 2025). Per the arXiv HTML (opened), Theorem 3.1 says a split graph with an independent set of size 4 (clique size arbitrary) is word-representable if and only if it contains none of nine minimal forbidden induced subgraphs: T1 to T8 and D1. The paper says this answers an open problem posed by Kitaev and Pyatkin, citing their IPL paper. Published as 'Characterization of word-representable split graphs with an independent set of fixed size' in Utilitas Mathematica 128 (2026), pages 3-31; received 30 Mar 2026, accepted 21 Jun 2026, published online 22 Jul 2026 (DOI 10.61091/um128-01), per the journal page (opened). The journal abstract still says partial progress has been made and a complete classification remains open, and its introduction, per the extract, aims at a complete list. The journal version's own scope is also described as 'split graphs with an independent set of size four'.
events.revisions: v1 only on arXiv (11 Jul 2025). Utilitas Mathematica 128 (2026), pp. 3-31, published online 22 Jul 2026 (journal version; the arXiv v1 is the first public argument).
events.delivers: Restricted to split graphs with independent set of size exactly 4: a finite minimal forbidden induced subgraph characterisation (T1 to T8 and D1) valid for every clique size. Says nothing for independent set size 5 and above, and nothing for non-split graphs.
events.remains: Split graphs with independent set of size 5 or more; all non-split graphs; the general characterisation. The journal version calls a complete classification of word-representable split graphs open.

events.directly_checkable: D1 is a single small graph, so non-word-representability can be checked by hand from the semi-transitive criterion, and the Pith review says the paper does not give an explicit adjacency for D1 and the key forcing step is not spelled out. I did not check the graph.
events.doubts: Pith review (automated, 6 Aug 2026), major objections: (1) the proof that D1 is non-word-representable is not rigorous, its key forcing step not spelled out; (2) minimality of D1 omits a symmetry justification; (3) completeness of the case analysis is not established, and several 'adding a vertex yields T_i' assertions are unproven; (4) the positive certificates are lists of orders never shown to satisfy the theorem's conditions. Six minor objections. Pith says no human expert has reviewed the paper; the journal acceptance implies a referee process I did not inspect. The Srinivasan preprint (below) claims a broader characterisation covering split graphs with this independent-set size, and the overlap is not compared in either paper.
events.direction: Cuts toward the forbidden-subgraph form for split graphs with independent set of size 4, as the question asks: a finite list of nine forbidden graphs claimed to characterise word-representability in that class. No counterexample to any conjecture.

The adjacency of D1 is not given in the extracted text (Pith says the paper does not give it explicitly). The claimed reason it is non-word-representable is the forcing argument the Pith review says is not spelled out.

events.what_happened: Chen, Hameed and Kitaev posted 'On the word-representability of K_m-K_n graphs' (arXiv 2508.15177, 21 Aug 2025). Per the arXiv abstract (opened), they study graphs whose vertices can be partitioned into two cliques, which is the same as co-bipartite graphs (the complement is bipartite), and give a complete characterisation of such word-representable graphs in terms of forbidden subgraphs when one of the cliques has size at most four. For clique size four they state there are seven minimal non-word-representable graphs. Published in Discussiones Mathematicae Graph Theory 46(2) (pp. 321-339), accepted 20 Aug 2025, published online 23 Sep 2025, per the Strathclyde record (opened).
events.revisions: v1 only on arXiv (21 Aug 2025). DMGT 46(2) 2026 issue; published online 23 Sep 2025.
events.delivers: A complete forbidden-subgraph characterisation of word-representable co-bipartite graphs where one clique has size at most 4, with seven minimal non-word-representable graphs for clique size 4 (the seven graphs themselves are not in the abstract). Restricted to co-bipartite graphs with a clique of size at most 4. The abstract does not say whether the characterisation holds for all sizes of the other clique.
events.remains: Co-bipartite graphs with both cliques of size 5 or more; the general characterisation. The Srinivasan preprint (below) gives an infinite-family result for all word-representable co-bipartite graphs, which would overlap this one.

events.what_happened: Das and Hariharasubramanian posted 'Word-representable co-bipartite graphs: vertex ordering, representation number, speed, and entropy' (arXiv 2509.03064; v1 3 Sep 2025, v2 2 Jun 2026). Per the arXiv abstract (opened), they give necessary and sufficient conditions, in terms of a vertex ordering, for a co-bipartite graph to be word-representable; the representation number is at most 3; permutation graphs are the co-bipartite graphs with representation number 2; the speed is 2^(O(n log n)) and the entropy is 0.

events.what_happened: Srinivasan and Hariharasubramanian posted 'Forbidden induced subgraph characterization of word-representable split graphs' (arXiv 2512.12259, 13 Dec 2025, v1 only). Per the arXiv HTML (opened), the abstract says the paper gives a complete forbidden submatrix characterisation of the I-circular property, which yields a characterisation of semi-transitive split graphs in terms of minimal forbidden induced subgraphs; and that the characterisation 'remains an open problem' beforehand. Theorem 4.1 says a split graph is semi-transitive iff its adjacency matrix has the I-circular property, derived from Kitaev and Pyatkin's Theorems 4 and 5. Theorem 4.4 characterises semi-transitive split graphs by forbidden induced subgraphs from a family 𝒢split in Figure 6. As extracted, that family is infinite: parameterised families M_I*(k) for k at least 3, M_II(k) for k at least 4, M_III(k) for k at least 3, and four further graphs M_IV to M_VII, with M_VII appearing only in the figure. The extraction does not show a finiteness claim. The paper cites Roy and Hariharasubramanian for the independent-set-4 case, without comparing the two lists.
events.revisions: v1 only (13 Dec 2025, per the arXiv abstract and HTML pages). Thesis version: Srinivasan, IIT Guwahati, Jan 2026 (catalogued May 2026; PDF behind login, not read).
events.delivers: For split graphs: as claimed by the authors, a forbidden-induced-subgraph characterisation of all semi-transitive (word-representable) split graphs, with the forbidden family given as infinite parameterised families (per extraction). Restricted to split graphs. Not a finite list as written, so its form is an infinite family, not a finite list.
events.remains: Non-split graphs; the general characterisation. Whether the family is minimal and complete, and how it relates to Roy and Hariharasubramanian's nine-graph list for independent set size 4, are not checked here.
events.directly_checkable: The forbidden graphs (T1 to T8, D1 and the M-families) are small explicit graphs, so minimality and the forbidden-subgraph claims can be checked by hand. I did not check any.
events.doubts: (1) Preprint only, no journal and no human review found. (2) Text extraction: M_VII appears only in a figure and is not defined in the text. (3) Its abstract calls the split-graph characterisation an open problem beforehand and presents its own result as resolving it. The body has to support that, and I checked only the extracted theorem statements. (4) The Utilitas journal version of the Roy paper (July 2026) cites this preprint as reference [13] but still says a complete list of minimal forbidden induced subgraphs for word-representable split graphs is a goal ('Toward the development of a complete list'), so the later author team does not treat this preprint as settling it. (5) The Pith review of this preprint could not be retrieved (HTTP 404). (6) The M-families are infinite as extracted, while Roy and Hariharasubramanian's nine-graph list covers independent set size 4 with all clique sizes; if any M-family member has an independent set of size 4, the two results must agree on it, and I did not check this.
events.direction: Cuts toward the forbidden-subgraph form for split graphs, with an infinite family of forbidden subgraphs as the claimed answer. It does not contradict the claim in the bullet. It is a claimed resolution for the restricted class of split graphs, and the general class remains open.
events.object: The forbidden family 𝒢split from Figure 6: infinite parameterised families M_I*(k) (k at least 3), M_II(k) (k at least 4), M_III(k) (k at least 3), and graphs M_IV to M_VII, each claimed to be a minimal non-semi-transitive split graph. The graphs themselves are not described in the extracted text.

events.what_happened: Srinivasan and Hariharasubramanian posted 'Forbidden induced subgraph characterization of word-representable co-bipartite graphs' (arXiv 2512.12274, 13 Dec 2025; v2 11 Apr 2026). Per the arXiv abstract (opened), they give a structural and algorithmic characterisation of word-representable co-bipartite graphs, show that a co-bipartite graph is a circle graph iff it is a permutation graph, derive a minimal forbidden induced subgraph characterisation for co-bipartite circle graphs, connect semi-transitivity with the circularly compatible ones property of binary matrices, and give a linear-time recognition algorithm. The HTML (v1) extraction gives Theorem 18: a co-bipartite graph is semi-transitive iff it contains no graph from a family 𝒢co, which is infinite as extracted (CG(M_I*(k)) and complements for k at least 3, plus CG(Z2*), CG(Z3*), CG(Z5) and CG(complement of Z2*)). The extraction also gives Corollary 8.1, a forbidden family 𝒢co^p for circle co-bipartite graphs, which contains complements of C_2k for k at least 3 plus three graphs. It cites Das and Hariharasubramanian for 'a complete characterization in terms of necessary and sufficient conditions'.
events.revisions: v1 13 Dec 2025; v2 11 Apr 2026 (per the arXiv abstract page). The HTML I opened was v1, so the v2 content is not known.
events.delivers: For co-bipartite graphs, per Theorem 18 as extracted and the abstract: a forbidden-induced-subgraph characterisation of all word-representable co-bipartite graphs, by an infinite family, and a forbidden family for the circle subclass (equal to the co-bipartite permutation graphs). Restricted to co-bipartite graphs.
events.remains: Non-co-bipartite graphs; the general characterisation. The circle subclass result is a further restriction inside the co-bipartite result.

disputes.summary: Srinivasan and Hariharasubramanian (arXiv 2512.12259, Dec 2025) present a complete forbidden-induced-subgraph characterisation of semi-transitive split graphs, with an infinite family. The later Roy and Hariharasubramanian journal version (Utilitas Mathematica 128, online 22 Jul 2026), which cites the Srinivasan preprint as reference [13], still says a complete list of minimal forbidden induced subgraphs for word-representable split graphs is a goal. Only one of these readings is consistent with the other, and I cannot tell which from the record.

Srinivasan and Hariharasubramanian (arXiv 2512.12274) state that 'a complete characterization in terms of necessary and sufficient conditions was later provided by Das and Hariharasubramanian', citing arXiv 2501.10112. The arXiv abstract of 2501.10112 gives necessary and sufficient conditions for semi-transitive orientation (no forbidden subgraphs), and its arXiv page lists only v1. The vertex-ordering characterisation is in arXiv 2509.03064 (v2 June 2026). Which paper is meant is not settled by what I read.

The Pith (AI-generated) summary of arXiv 2512.12274 reads its central result as 'word-representable iff circle iff permutation' for co-bipartite graphs. The extracted Theorem 18 of the same paper is a separate infinite family for word-representability, and Corollary 8.1 is a separate family for circle graphs. These cannot both be read as the same equivalence without a check of the paper's full text.

Roy and Hariharasubramanian (arXiv 2507.08483) give a finite list of nine forbidden graphs for split graphs with independent set size 4, for all clique sizes. Srinivasan and Hariharasubramanian (arXiv 2512.12259) give infinite families for all split graphs. The later paper cites the earlier one but does not compare the independent-set-4 case. Whether the two agree on that case is unchecked.

summary: The bullet asks for a forbidden-subgraph characterisation of all word-representable graphs. Every source I opened treats that general problem as open. Wikipedia's list of open problems includes this exact item, with the page last edited 9 August 2026. Kenkireth, Sajith and Sasidharan's preprint (v4, June 2026) says the characterisation for word-representable graphs remains open. The July 2026 journal version of Roy and Hariharasubramanian's split-graph paper says a complete classification remains open. Event-level evidence in the window is restricted-class work. The strongest results are: Roy and Hariharasubramanian (arXiv July 2025; journal Utilitas Mathematica online July 2026) give a finite list of nine forbidden split graphs for independent set size 4; Chen, Hameed and Kitaev (arXiv August 2025; DMGT 2025/26) give a complete forbidden list for co-bipartite graphs with one clique of size at most 4; Srinivasan and Hariharasubramanian (arXiv December 2025, two preprints, no journal found) claim forbidden-induced-subgraph characterisations of all semi-transitive split graphs and of all word-representable co-bipartite graphs, each as an infinite family as extracted. Their split-graph claim is the closest to a result on the general question, and it is restricted to split graphs. Earlier work since 2017 (Kitaev, Long, Ma, Wu; Chen, Kitaev, Saito; Kitaev and Pyatkin; Akgün et al.) covers the same restricted classes or gives census results up to 11 vertices. Neighbouring 2024-2026 work (square-free words, circulants, products, line graphs, representation numbers, melon graphs, 2-word-π and language-representability) does not bear on the forbidden-subgraph form. Automated AI referee reviews on Pith (reviewer model deepseek-v4-flash for the Roy split-graph paper and the Chen, Hameed and Kitaev co-bipartite paper; grok-4.3 for the December 2025 co-bipartite preprint) raise gaps in each. They check the papers and do not contribute to the mathematics, so ai.none_found is false on those events while ai.systems stays empty. No source credits an AI system with any part of the mathematics, and my searches found none. A close call is whether the December 2025 split-graph preprint should count as moving the general quantity. It settles one restricted class, is not peer reviewed as far as I found, and its own journal successor in July 2026 does not treat the complete list as done. On the scope test in section 2.1 I read it as moving a restricted class only. The second close call is the co-bipartite December 2025 preprint, whose Theorem 18 covers all word-representable co-bipartite graphs with an infinite family, and whose attribution and circle-graph equivalence are unclear.
competing_reading: The strongest case for a larger move: Srinivasan and Hariharasubramanian (arXiv 2512.12259 and 2512.12274) present complete forbidden-induced-subgraph characterisations for two of the main restricted classes (all split graphs and all co-bipartite graphs). Together with the Roy and Chen results, the problem could be read as settled class by class, so that only the non-split, non-co-bipartite graphs remain. The bullet's wording does not require a finite list, so an infinite family would meet its form. A reader could take this to move the problem substantially. The case against: each result is restricted to one class, the claims are preprints with no human review found, the split-graph family is infinite as extracted and its minimality is unchecked, and the later journal version of the split-graph paper still treats the complete list as open. Under the scope test in section 2.1, none of these restricted results is a characterisation of all word-representable graphs.
what_would_settle_it: (1) A full-text check of arXiv 2512.12259 Theorem 4.4 and Figure 6: whether the families are complete and minimal, whether M_VII is defined, and whether any member has independent set size 4, to test against Roy and Hariharasubramanian's nine-graph list. (2) A full-text check of 2512.12274 Theorem 18 against its own v2 (April 2026), and whether the word-representable and circle families differ as the extraction indicates. (3) Any refereed publication or human review of either December 2025 preprint, and the referee reports for Utilitas Mathematica 128 (Roy and Hariharasubramanian). (4) Any paper from 2026 that either cites 2512.12259 and says the split-graph list is complete, or says it is not. (5) A paper that characterises all word-representable graphs by forbidden induced subgraphs, or shows the minimal list is infinite. None of these was found.

event.what_happened: Kenkireth, Sajith and Sasidharan posted 'Word-representability and comparability: minimal forbidden induced subgraphs and cover number bounds'. Per the arXiv abstract (opened), they identify which minimal non-comparability graphs are also minimal non-word-representable; they give a complete description of minimal non-word-representable graphs containing an all-adjacent vertex; they show the universal O(log n) cover-number bound for word-representable graphs by comparability graphs is tight. The abstract says the characterisation for word-representable graphs remains open.

Scope that changed between versions is a point for the later pass.

judgement.why: The statement asks for a forbidden-subgraph characterisation of all word-representable graphs; it names no subclass, so every forbidden-subgraph characterisation of a restricted class (split graphs with independent set size 4, co-bipartite with a clique of size at most 4, all split graphs, all co-bipartite graphs, graphs with an all-adjacent vertex) is a case. Co-bipartite results stated as orientation or vertex-ordering conditions rather than forbidden subgraphs answer a changed question and are variant, as are the neighbouring results on word lengths, square-freeness, circulants, line graphs, melon graphs, representation numbers and generalised representability. Censuses and individual certificates are instances. Roy-Hariharasubramanian and Chen-Hameed-Kitaev are accepted by journals of record, so digested; the Pith AI-referee objections are automated and neither digest nor knock down (F8). The December 2025 Srinivasan preprints are unreviewed and doubtful because the later journal paper from an overlapping team still treats the split list as open. Hefty et al. has only a 2024 year date, so after_snapshot is null. Pith reviews are the only AI involvement, and they criticise, so ai_role is none throughout.
judgement.doubts: Whether the Srinivasan split and co-bipartite families are complete and minimal is unresolved in the record; the co-bipartite infinite-family claim is internally inconsistent with the Pith summary. Journal referee processes were not inspected. No date-filtered arXiv sweep was run.
